question: An engineer must implement private VLANs for a group of Cisco UCS B-Series servers. The primary VLAN is present, but the secondary VLAN must be added to both fabrics. Which configuration set accomplishes this task?
options:
UCS-A# scope eth-uplink -
UCS-A /eth-uplink # create vlan vlan1981 1981
UCS-A /eth-uplink/vlan* # set sharing none

UCS-A# scope eth-uplink -
UCS-A /eth-uplink # create vlan vlan1981 1981
UCS-A /eth-uplink/vlan* # set sharing isolated

UCS-A# scope eth-uplink -
UCS-A /eth-uplink # scope fabric a
UCS-A /eth-uplink/fabric # create vlan vlan1981 1981
UCS-A /eth-uplink/fabric/vlan* # set sharing secondary

UCS-A# scope eth-uplink -
UCS-A /eth-uplink # scope fabric a
UCS-A /eth-uplink/fabric # create vlan vlan1981 1981
UCS-A /eth-uplink/fabric/vlan* # set sharing private
theory: Private VLANs use a primary VLAN paired with one or more secondary VLANs (isolated or community) to segment hosts that share a subnet but should not communicate directly with each other. To add the secondary VLAN so it is available on both fabrics, it is created as a normal VLAN object under 'scope eth-uplink' (not scoped under a single fabric) and marked with 'set sharing isolated,' which designates it as an isolated secondary VLAN paired to the primary — 'sharing none' would make it an ordinary VLAN rather than a PVLAN secondary, and 'sharing secondary'/'sharing private' are not valid keyword values. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Network Management, Private VLANs)
